title: Guidelines on Duration of Medical Leave for Specific Injuries
what_it_is: Guidelines on Duration of Medical Leave for Specific Injuries

sections.label: Medical leave and WICA reporting
sections.summary: The Ethical Code requires patient welfare first and medical leave based on clinical assessment; new WICA reporting should reduce inadequate leave, so guidelines are not needed now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Singapore Medical Council's Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG) requires the doctor to place the patient's welfare above all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Regarding medical leave, the doctor has to ensure that the duration and type of leave granted are based on medical grounds arrived at through proper clinical assessment by doctors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The duration of medical leave is determined by a variety of factors, including the type and severity of the injury, the period required for the treatment, rehabilitation and recovery, and the specific work requirements and workplace conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Recent changes in the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) to require employers to report any instance of employees on medical leave or light duties due to a work injury, when effected, should reduce the risk of inadequate medical leave.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Therefore, for now, we do not think that guidelines for medical leave on work-related injuries are necessary.

sections.label: SMC guidelines and WICA reporting
sections.summary: Consultations and surveys abroad show prescriptive guidelines are difficult, so SMC issued 2017 general guidelines; new WICA reporting from September should minimise under-prescribing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Indeed, we have done some preliminary consultations as well as done a survey of the landscape of such issues in various countries, like New Zealand, Australia and the United Kingdom.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: All these vary very greatly, and it is actually difficult to have a set of prescriptive guidelines for prescribing medical leave and even light duties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, that is the reason why the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), in 2017, did issue some general guidelines on what doctors should take into account, as I have enumerated earlier, as well as the fact that they should not take into account extraneous factors like who is going to benefit, who is going to pay, impact on insurance claims and so on, as well as to consult their peers where they may not be sure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We think that with the new WICA coming into effect from September of this year, where even light duties given – even if it is one day – will have to be reported, that will actually minimise this issue of under prescribing medical leave or light duties.
